nodes.label: codeql workflow
nodes.rationale: Until it landed, code-scanning answered 404 no analysis found - the repository had never been analysed once (#539). Everything here parses somebody else's bytes: cluster wire frames, HOCON, HTTP requests and WebSocket payloads, persisted snapshots - exactly the input surface CodeQL's default queries are written for, and no other gate looks for a taint path. Runs on PRs so a finding attaches to the change that introduced it, on long-lived branches so the baseline stays current, and weekly because CodeQL ships new queries and a file clean in March can be flagged in June untouched. javascript-typescript is one language covering .ts/.mts/.mjs/.js; build-mode: none extracts from source, so no dependency install.

nodes.label: Deliberately no paths filter
nodes.rationale: Unlike build.yml and package-health.yml. Code scanning treats the newest analysis of a branch as the truth about that branch, so skipping a push would leave the alert set describing a commit that is no longer there.

nodes.label: Job-level security-events: write
nodes.rationale: A read-only floor for the file with the one write scope declared on the analyze job alone (#621) - the rule WorkflowHygiene.test.ts enforces, and the reason docs.yml's build job used to hold scopes it never used. Uploading the SARIF is what makes an alert appear; the category keys the upload so a second language could not silently replace this analysis. timeout-minutes: 30 rather than the 6 h default, since a runaway analysis holding a runner for six hours is not a useful failure mode.
